Accuracy in an Italian lexical decision task

Source: R/data.R
lexical_accuracy.Rd

30 native speakers of Italian decide whether each of 60 Italian words is a word; the outcome is whether the response was correct. For mixed-effects logistic regression.

Usage

lexical_accuracy

Format

A tibble with 1800 rows and 5 columns:

participant

Participant ID, P01 to P30.

word

Word ID, w01 to w60.

log_freq

log10 word frequency, 1 to 6.

freq_c

log_freq, centred on the mean of the 60 words.

correct

1 for a correct response, 0 for an error.

Source

data-raw/lexical_accuracy.R

Details

True model, in log-odds: 1.5 + u0 + w0 + (0.8 + u1) * freq_c. By-participant intercepts u0 have SD 0.8 and slopes u1 SD 0.3 (uncorrelated); by-word intercepts w0 have SD 0.5.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("lme4", quietly = TRUE)) {
  m <- lme4::glmer(correct ~ freq_c + (1 + freq_c || participant) + (1 | word),
                   data = lexical_accuracy, family = binomial)
  summary(m)
}
